# Lab 15.5: Discover PII with Data Profiles

## What We Are Going to Do
Load a table with fake personal data into BigQuery, turn on Sensitive Data Protection discovery, and read the data profile it creates.

## Steps

1. **Create a table with fake PII.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq mk --dataset --location=US $PROJECT_ID:sdp_lab

cat &gt; customers.csv &lt;&lt;EOF
name,email,phone,card,country
Asha Rao,asha@example.com,415-555-0100,4111111111111111,US
Ravi Patel,ravi@example.com,415-555-0101,5555555555554444,IN
Mia Chen,mia@example.com,415-555-0102,378282246310005,US
EOF

bq load --source_format=CSV --skip_leading_rows=1 \
  sdp_lab.customers customers.csv \
  name:STRING,email:STRING,phone:STRING,card:STRING,country:STRING</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **Enable the API.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable dlp.googleapis.com</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **Turn on discovery for BigQuery.** In the console go to **Security → Sensitive Data Protection → Discovery → Enable** (or **Create scan configuration**). Choose **BigQuery**, scope **Scan selected project**, and pick your project.

4. **Choose where results go.** Tick **Publish to Security Command Center** and **Save data profile copies to BigQuery** in a dataset such as `sdp_lab_profiles`. Keep the default schedule and create the configuration.

5. **Wait for the profile.** The first profiles can take up to a few hours. Then open **Discovery → Data profiles → Tables**.

6. **Read the profile** for `sdp_lab.customers`:
   - **Sensitivity**: High
   - **Data risk**: based on sensitivity and access
   - **InfoTypes**: `EMAIL_ADDRESS`, `PHONE_NUMBER`, `CREDIT_CARD_NUMBER`, `PERSON_NAME`
   - Column-level profiles show which column holds which type

7. **Clean up.** Delete the scan configuration in **Discovery**, then:

<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">

bq rm -r -f --dataset $PROJECT_ID:sdp_lab_profiles</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Table sensitivity | High |
| Columns | Each mapped to the infoType found |
| Continuous | New tables are profiled automatically |
| Results | Visible in SDP, SCC and BigQuery |
